title: Scheme-theoretic image
statement:
Let $g\colon T\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes. Its *kernel ideal*
$\ker(g)\subseteq\mathcal O_Y$ is the largest quasi-coherent ideal
contained in the kernel of $\mathcal O_Y\to g_*\mathcal O_T$ (this kernel
itself when $g$ is quasi-compact). The *scheme-theoretic image*
$\operatorname{SIm}(g)$ of $g$ is the closed subscheme of $Y$ defined by
$\ker(g)$, with inclusion
$g_{\mathrm{im}}\colon\operatorname{SIm}(g)\hookrightarrow Y$ and factor map
$g^{\mathrm{im}}\colon T\to\operatorname{SIm}(g)$ as in
[lemma-nagata-scheme-image-ideal-qc]. A morphism $g\colon T\to Y$ is
*scheme-theoretically dense* if its scheme-theoretic image is $Y$ itself,
i.e. $\ker(g)=0$. The scheme-theoretic closure of a locally closed
subscheme is the scheme-theoretic image of its immersion.

mathlib_match.how: One declaration per clause, all read in the pinned checkout. Kernel ideal: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.ker, Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/IdealSheaf/Basic.lean:692, is IdealSheafData.ofIdeals of the affine section kernels; IdealSheafData.ofIdeals:104 and le_ofIdeals_iff:125 give exactly the largest quasi-coherent ideal contained in those kernels. Under QuasiCompact g, Scheme.Hom.ker_apply, Basic.lean:702, identifies it with the ordinary sheaf kernel on the affine basis. Image and inclusion: Scheme.Hom.image and Scheme.Hom.imageι, Subscheme.lean:662 and :665, are g.ker.subscheme and its closed immersion. Factor map and equality: Scheme.Hom.toImage and Scheme.Hom.toImage_imageι, Subscheme.lean:710 and :715, require no quasi-compactness. Density: AlgebraicGeometry.IsSchemeTheoreticallyDominant, Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/SchemeTheoreticallyDominant.lean:38, is by definition g.ker = bottom; Scheme.isIso_subschemeι_iff_eq_bot, Subscheme.lean:735, is exactly the equivalence with the image inclusion being an isomorphism. Closure of a locally closed subscheme is the one-line specialization Scheme.Hom.image i to its immersion i, with inclusion i.imageι. Thus every clause is an existing definition or direct single-lemma identification, with quasi-compactness used only for the ordinary-kernel parenthesis.

blueprint_sketch.statement:
Let $g\colon T\to Y$ be a morphism. Define
$\operatorname{SIm}(g)$ to mean the Mathlib scheme-theoretic image
`Scheme.Hom.image g`, with inclusion $g_{\mathrm{im}}$ and factor map
$g^{\mathrm{im}}$ supplied by
[lemma-nagata-scheme-image-ideal-qc]. Whenever a later argument needs
quasi-compactness, it must state that hypothesis explicitly.
